title: Reasons for Rise in Recidivism Rate at Drug Rehabilitation Centre Inmates
what_it_is: Reasons for Rise in Recidivism Rate at Drug Rehabilitation Centre Inmates

sections.label: Drug rehabilitation regime change
sections.summary: MHA changed the regime in 2019 so third-time abusers go to the DRC instead of prosecution, and repeat abusers in DRC release cohorts rose from about 35% in 2020 to 54% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) changed the drug rehabilitation regime such that abusers who are arrested for the third and subsequent times are sent to the Drug Rehabilitation Centre (DRC) for rehabilitation, instead of being prosecuted and subject to an extended imprisonment term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Since this change, the proportion of repeat drug abusers in the DRC release cohorts has increased from about 35% for the 2020 release cohort to 54% for the 2022 release cohort.

sections.label: Re-integration Hub for release
sections.summary: SPS recently established the Re-integration Hub to centralise the pre-emplacement regime for drug abusers scheduled for release on community-based programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, to better prepare drug abusers for release, SPS recently established the Re-integration Hub to centralise the pre-emplacement regime for drug abusers who are scheduled for release on community-based programmes.

sections.label: CNB drug syndicates dismantled
sections.summary: Last year, CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates and made significant drug seizures with an estimated market value of about $13.5 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Last year, CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates and made significant drug seizures with an estimated market value of about $13.5 million.

sections.label: Recidivism of inmates with drug antecedents
sections.summary: Inmates with previous drug antecedents are about three times more likely to reoffend, and the 2018 release cohort with drug antecedents had a 29.9% recidivism rate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Indeed, based on the two-year recidivism rate, inmates with previous drug antecedents are approximately three times more likely to reoffend than those without.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: When we look at the recidivism rate for the release cohort in 2018, for those with drug antecedents, it was 29.9%.

sections.label: Preventive drug education programmes
sections.summary: The community works upstream to prevent drug taking through extensive preventive drug education programmes, the Inter-Ministry Committee on Drug Prevention for Youths, and Dadah Itu Haram programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: That is why we go upstream to work with the community to see how we can prevent anyone, even one person, from taking drugs, because we know drugs are harmful.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have extensive preventive drug education programmes and then, recently, we launched the Inter-Ministry Committee on Drug Prevention for Youths, and we have organisations coming onboard to help us with Dadah Itu Haram programmes.

sections.label: Re-integration Hub programmes
sections.summary: The Re-integration Hub brings in programmes relating to employment, improving social esteem, and fostering a sense of belonging.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, that is why we have the Re-integration Hub, where we bring in programmes relating to employment, relating to how they can improve their social esteem and also how they can feel they have a sense of belonging.
